edges.rationale: Sivananda’s disciple Sahajananda carried Divine Life Society service into South Africa. SPN holds records for both. A neighbouring display or cross-reference can show how this Himalayan teaching community became an international service network.

Dilip Kumar Roy, represented in SPN’s Bengal group, wrote a first-person account of visiting Ramana in 1945. This is a personal encounter linking two displays; preserve his own teaching relationship with Sri Aurobindo separately.

Mahendranath Gupta, Ramakrishna’s disciple and recorder, personally guided the young Yogananda, as Yogananda recounts in his autobiography. Put the M. end of the Ramakrishna group toward the Kriya display. Anandamayi Ma’s meeting with Yogananda offers another named connection.
Keep the Sai connections together. Kaleshwar’s reported visionary guidance from Shirdi Sai provides context for the connections between the southern and western displays.
Use this shared context area to introduce international spiritual communities. Keep each community identifiable; place confirmed Bhakti Marga members together. This is a proposed display adjacency.
Sadhu Vaswani and Dada J. P. Vaswani visited Ramana together in 1939. Keep the teacher–disciple pair together and use their meeting with Ramana to connect the two display areas.

Keep Omkarnath’s immediate lineage coherent in the East; retain cross-tradition context. His relationship with Parankush Ramanuj is a named guru–disciple connection, not a reason to divide the family between displays.
